name: Sustaining Change Over Years
title: Sustaining Change Over Years
answer: Sustaining change over years means building lasting habits of governance, measurement, and honest reporting so that AI adoption survives constant changes in tools and in school leadership. The habits matter more than any particular product, and written rules, published results, and broad committees help practices outlast turnover. Districts should revisit their AI strategy at least once a year, using the annual report as a natural moment for honest review.

sections.body: AI tools will keep changing, and the rules and practices in this Volume will need updating, so a district that builds strong habits of governance, measurement, and honest reporting will adapt more easily than one that chases each new tool. The habits matter more than any particular product, and they are what make adoption last. Leadership turnover is a threat to lasting change, because a new superintendent or principal may abandon what came before. Written rules, published results, and a committee with broad membership help practices survive changes in leadership, and so does a staff that understands why the practices matter. The problem this solves is the fragility of adoption that depends on one leader or one tool rather than on durable routines.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: Districts should revisit their AI strategy at least once a year, and the annual report described in the book is a natural moment for this review. At that review, leaders can ask what worked, what did not, what has changed in the tools and the law, and what to do next. Steady, honest review keeps adoption on track. The text does not give separate grade band examples for this idea, so the practice applies at the district and school level rather than by classroom age group. The work rests on written rules, published results, and a committee with broad membership, alongside a staff that understands why the practices matter.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea, so it rests on practice rather than research. The book presents sustaining change over years as guidance drawn from experience about governance, measurement, and honest reporting, not as a claim backed by a named study. Its evidence label is therefore practice based, and the reasoning offered is that habits outlast products and that written rules, published results, and broad committees help practices survive leadership turnover.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits and risks here are leadership turnover and the temptation to chase each new tool instead of keeping durable habits. A new superintendent or principal may abandon what came before, which is why written rules, published results, and a committee with broad membership matter, and why a staff that understands the reasons behind the practices matters too. The decisions that stay with people are the annual review choices: what worked, what did not, what has changed in the tools and the law, and what to do next. The text does not say that any product or single leader can secure lasting change, and it places the responsibility for honest reporting and steady review with district and school leaders.
